title: How tanks are scored
html:
A tank has two jobs: hold aggro so your DPS can go all out, and stay alive. We sim each tank on six raid bosses and measure both:

  • Safe DPS: how much DPS a damage dealer can do behind this tank without pulling aggro.
  • Healing needed: how much healing per second the tank needs to stay alive.

The score turns both into one number, in raid DPS. More threat lets the raid do more damage. Needing more healing costs the raid: each extra healer on the tank takes a slot that could hold a DPS player.

The three setups weigh these differently. Max threat cares most about aggro, Max survival most about needing less healing, and Balanced weighs them evenly. Higher is better. A score can go below zero, mostly at Max survival, where healing counts three times as much.

title: Safe DPS
html: Aggro trouble mostly comes in the first seconds of a pull, before the tank has built a lead. So Safe DPS isn't the tank's average threat: it's the steady DPS a player can do, starting 2 seconds after the pull, without ever going over the tank's threat, even at the worst moment of the fight. You pull aggro at 110% of the tank's threat, as in melee range. Forever has no Blessing of Salvation, so every point of your damage is a point of threat.

title: Healing needed
html:
On each boss the tank gets a steady stream of heals, as often as real raids heal their main tank. We turn that healing down until the tank dies in 1 fight out of 20. That amount, in HPS, is the healing it needs.

It counts everything that keeps a tank alive: armor, avoidance, health and blocks. Spiky damage counts too: a tank that takes big hits needs more healing than one that takes the same damage in small ones.

Sometimes no amount of healing is enough, when the boss kills the tank between two heals too often. Then healing needed shows none and the score drops far below the rest.

title: The bosses
html:
Six bosses count toward the score, with the damage and healing real 40-player raids had on them (Warcraft Logs of the Anniversary realms). Forever's own raids have no logs yet, so these Classic bosses stand in. Each fight is the time the main tank spends on the boss.

  • Magmadar (53 sec): Fast swings, with his Frenzy counted as often as real raids let it through. Lava Breath is in. His fear, Magma Spit and Lava Bomb are left out.
  • Golemagg the Incinerator (56 sec): Golemagg only: his two Core Ragers are another tank's job. Magma Splash stacks Fire damage on you (a steady 4 stacks here); its armor loss is left out, and so are Earthquake and Pyroblast.
  • Onyxia (35 sec): The ground phases only: her air phase is left out. Knock Away's threat loss and Bellowing Roar's fear aren't in.
  • Broodlord Lashlayer (41 sec): The hardest boss to keep a tank alive on: big hits, and Mortal Strike halves your healing for 5 seconds. Blast Wave is in. Knock Away's threat loss isn't.
  • Vaelastrasz the Corrupt (17 sec): One tank's stretch before Burning Adrenaline forces a swap, so a short fight. Flame Breath's burn stacks up to 5 times, and fire resistance helps.
  • Chromaggus (1 min 55 sec): Incinerate and Corrosive Acid as his breaths, and his Frenzy counted as often as raids let it through. Corrosive Acid's armor loss is left out.
  • Ragnaros (1 min 11 sec): Shown, not scored. Elemental Fire burns you on most of his hits, and it's one tank's time between his knockbacks. Real raids tank him in fire resistance gear, which these setups don't wear, so every tank needs far more healing here than raids give.

title: What the sim leaves out
html:
• Threat drops, like Onyxia's and Broodlord's Knock Away.
  • Buttons for when you're low: Last Stand, Shield Wall when you're low, health potions, Lay on Hands. Defensive cooldowns are used on cooldown or at a set time instead.
  • Healers reacting to you: the heals come at a steady pace whatever your health.
  • Adds and tank swaps: one tank on the boss.

title: The exact math
html:
On each boss:

Score = 2 × Safe DPS − weight × 900 × healing needed ÷ one healer's HPS

  • 2 × Safe DPS: the two DPS players closest to the tank's threat can both go that fast.
  • Healing needed ÷ one healer's HPS: how many healers the tank needs. One healer's HPS is what each healer on the main tank healed in real kills of that boss, from about 170 to about 710.
  • 900: the DPS a player would add in that healer's slot.
  • Weight: ⅓ for Max threat, 1 for Balanced, 3 for Max survival.

The score is the average over the six bosses. The ± next to a number is how far it could move by luck: two setups closer than that are about even.
